newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks close slightly up, helped by Wall St.
newsitem.headline: French stocks close slightly up, helped by Wall St.

text.p: French shares closed slightly higher after having spent most of the day in the red, following afternoon support by a higher Wall Street market.
The U.S. markets were boosted by the November personal income data. Paris had suffered earlier from profit-taking on the last day of the December account
The blue-chip CAC-40 index was up 8.91 points or 0.39 percent at 2,287.44 while the CAC-40 futures contract was up at 2,296.5 from 2,280 on Friday's close.
Volume was 6.83 billion francs, of which 3.81 billion francs was in CAC-40 stocks.
The December account closed with a gain of 1.42 percent for the CAC-40 while the 1996 trading year ended with a 24.7 percent rise.
Traders said there were a big number of block deals, in AXA, Bic, Elf and Rhone-Poulenc.
"Some fund managers are adjusting their portfolios. It seems the end-of-year window dressing has started," a dealer said.
* Renault rallied 6.63 percent to 111 francs despite its chairman telling the La Tribune newspaper loss trend is accentuating and 1997 European market will be difficult.
* A trader explained the contrarian price reaction on Renault by saying "the market likes to be told the truth."
* Sanofi closed down 2.86 percent at 510 francs after a good rally last week when majority-owner Elf said a merger of the pharmaceuticals company was desirable.
* Roussel-Uclaf, unchanged at 1,510, traded in big 948 million franc turnover on the back of buy-out bid by Hoechst.

* Danone, up 0.7 percent to 724, was not affected by the decision of its Panzani-William Saurin unit to recall deep-frozen meals which could contain British beef from before the import ban for mad cow disease.
* Moulinex falls 4.51 percent to 116.50 on reduced first half loss and plans for a 500 million franc cash call.

* Suez, up 0.80 percent to 214.70 franc, said it was in talks to sell its 50.8 percent stake in salt company Compagnie des Salins du Midi et des Salines de l'Est to Morton International Inc of the U.S. The French salt maker was suspended at 440 francs.

Suez on Saturday said it had accelerated the sale of Banque Indosuez to Credit Agricole and would get 5.6 billion francs in cash for the remaining 49 percent. It will make a 300 million franc capital gain in the 1996 results.
* Metaleurop down 10.78 percent at 42.20 after announcing plans for 600 million franc capital increase.

* Havas Advertising gained 1.08 percent to 561 francs on the back of remarks by chairman Alain de Pouzilhac to the Journal de Finances saying he expected a doubling of profits between now and three years.
